name: TDC ADMET CYP2C9_Veith
description: Predict whether a compound inhibits the drug-metabolising enzyme cytochrome P450 2C9 (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint CYP2C9_Veith of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the precision-recall curve on the test compounds, with class 1 as the positive class, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.

sources.locator: Comprehensive characterization of cytochrome P450 isozyme selectivity across chemical libraries
CYP P450 2C9/2D6/3A4 Inhibition, Veith et al.: binary classification, 12,092 / 13,130 / 12,328 drugs.

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the precision-recall curve (class 1 positive) on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

checks: leaderboard rank 1 (AUPRC): MapLight + GNN Jim Notwell 0.859

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: Veith et al. measured the inhibition of these isozymes by thousands of compounds, which is the property the task predicts; the paper's main objective is the characterisation of isozyme inhibition.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify molecules as inhibitors or non-inhibitors of the cytochrome P450 isozyme CYP2C9 from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: CYP2C9 is one of the main drug-metabolising enzymes; its inhibition by a co-administered drug raises the exposure of other drugs and causes drug-drug interactions, so inhibition is screened for early.

papers.title: Comprehensive characterization of cytochrome P450 isozyme selectivity across chemical libraries
papers.task_relation: The task predicts, from structure, the inhibition label of the isozyme named in the task, which this screen measured for about 12,000 compounds; the paper's own aim is the measurement, not a predictor, and the local split and metric are different.
papers.primary_goal: Measure the inhibition of five major cytochrome P450 isozymes by about 17,000 compounds in a quantitative high-throughput screen and characterise isozyme selectivity.
